gappers.catalyst_detail: Q3 (Nov 12) delivered revenue $980.8M, +571% YoY and ahead of consensus, with adjusted net income turning positive at +$90.9M from a -$100.4M adjusted loss a year earlier. The market traded the guidance instead: Nebius lowered the top end of FY26 revenue guidance, attributed data-centre capacity delays, and raised capex toward ~$45B. Shares fell -20.25% Nov 12 and -9.92% Nov 13, with Baird cutting $340->$200 and BofA ->$265. Today extends the slide to a fifth session at $106.60, ~64.4% below the $299.72 52-week high. A fresh news search bounded to Nov 14 onward returned zero results, confirming no new information today.
gappers.why: Beat the quarter, broke the story. Revenue growth was never the swing factor; a guidance cut plus capacity delays plus a ~$45B capex number converts the thesis from self-funding compounder to capital-hungry builder with execution risk - and it landed into Huang's NVIDIA resignation, which de-rated every Nvidia-backed neocloud at once. With no new catalyst today, the incremental move is positioning and sector beta, not information.
gappers.impact: Most damaged chart in the scan and a sustained de-rating, not a spike to fade: -29.5% vs 20-SMA, -45.2% vs 50-SMA, -40.6% vs 200-SMA, on prior-session volume of 48.9M. The five-session path 154.90 -> 128.91 -> 115.84 -> (Mon) 106.60 is -31.2%. Read-through is identical to CRWV - one trade expressed twice, not two independent signals.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: The guidance reset is structural but structurally bearish; a long thesis needs the capex and capacity-delay questions answered first, and XLK fails sector momentum on both 1mo and 3mo.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Account is flat ($100,000, 0 positions), so nothing is displaced - the real cost is one of three weekly trade slots. Huang's exit removes the perceived Nvidia backstop for exactly that vendor-financed model, so the market reprices the structure regardless of the backlog beat.

Huang's resignation and the neocloud de-rate dragged the whole AI-power complex down with the chips and the clouds - which is why a company that raised guidance and signed 900MW is down double digits in five sessions. BW at rank 7 is the same trade in a lower-quality wrapper, confirming the driver is sectoral rather than company-specific.

gappers.catalyst_detail: The 08:08 entry recorded 'no company news' for KLIC. That is now corrected: KLIC is expanding its Advanced Solutions production footprint in Singapore to support about US$400M in segment revenue by early fiscal 2027 - and the coverage frames it explicitly as capacity being added 'even as semiconductor and memory capital spending shows signs of cooling', i.e. the market is reading the expansion as risk rather than as a win. KLIC supplies the thermocompression and advanced-packaging bonders used in HBM and AI-accelerator assembly, and reports fiscal Q4 2026 on Wednesday Nov 18. The last reported quarter (fiscal Q3) was exceptional: revenue $330.4M (+122.6% YoY), gross margin 47.8%, operating profit $68.3M (+1,220%), net income $57.4M (+1,845.7%). Wednesday's consensus is refined to $1.43 EPS on $376.80M revenue (vs the ~$384M used at 08:08). Valuation views are violently split: analyst consensus fair value $95 against a Simply Wall St DCF of $48.73 - i.e. the sell side calls it ~46% undervalued and the DCF calls it ~25% overvalued at $65.
gappers.why: Pre-earnings positioning inside a sector-wide de-rate, now with a company-specific negative read attached. KLIC is advanced-packaging capex beta, so it trades on the same AI-capex doubt as the neoclouds and the power names - but the Singapore expansion gives the bears a concrete hook: committing capacity into cooling memory/semi capex is exactly the execution risk the de-rate is pricing. Holders who rode +93.6% are de-risking ahead of a number that has to clear a very high bar, and AMKR at rank 8 is the same packaging trade already punished for exactly that, having missed Q3 and guided Q4 soft.
gappers.impact: A sustained de-rate, not a spike to fade: five consecutive down sessions, -11.3% vs 20-SMA, -20.8% vs 50-SMA, -25.3% vs 200-SMA, and -32.1% over 90 days despite still being up ~42.9% YTD. Sector read-through is explicit and confirmatory - AMKR gapped -5.23% on the same driver and its Oct 26 miss is a live preview of the risk in KLIC's Wednesday print. Liquidity is adequate: prior-session consolidated volume 698k shares (~$45M notional), so a $10-20k clip is immaterial - though the IEX-only 20d average of ~36k shares badly understates the real book, and a limit order remains mandatory. Note the price has been pinned at exactly $65.00 across both the 08:08 and 09:09 scans, which for a 698k-share name is more likely a thin pre-market quote than genuine stability - treat the level as soft.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: The underlying advanced-packaging growth is genuinely structural, but with earnings two days out the tradeable horizon is dominated by a binary event, and the thesis cannot be underwritten until Wednesday's number and guide are known - now less, not more, attractive given the expansion-into-cooling-capex read.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Still the one row with a real argument rather than a flat rejection, and the best ATR fit in the scan: at 6.90% of price the 10% stop is 1.45 ATR and the +20% target 2.90 ATR - the only row where the stop sits comfortably outside one average day's range, and the closest any gapper has come to the mid-vol passing band identified in today's pre-market entry. It still fails on four independent counts: price is 25.3% below its 200-SMA, so the long-bias filter fails outright; price is below the 20-SMA while XLK is worst sector on 1mo and 3mo, so Rule 9 fails; fiscal Q4 earnings land Wednesday, an uncompensated binary two days out and immediately after NVDA's; and the newly surfaced Singapore read-through makes the print riskier, not safer. Within today's list it dominates all seven other rows on R:R shape - so if any gapper is ever worth a slot it is this one - but the correct action is to spend no slot today and re-examine after Wednesday's print, with a reclaim of the ~$73 20-SMA as the minimum technical precondition. Research only, no order.
